reason: While the text depicts the Israelites in distress and afraid (they see the pursuing Egyptians and cry out in fear), the narrative does not attribute their suffering to their own fault. Rather, their suffering results from Pharaoh's pursuit, which occurs after God commanded the exodus. The people's complaints to Moses express doubts and a wish to return to servitude, but these complaints are not framed as the cause of their immediate suffering. Instead, the text presents the situation as a test of faith in which God himself will fight for them and deliver them. The suffering is presented as external (Pharaoh's pursuit) and overcome by divine intervention, not as a consequence of the people's wrongdoing.
